questions.question: Pandit Jasraj, Bhimsen Joshi and Zakir Hussain are associated with which form of music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindustani Classical Music**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question: Which of the following can be referred to in the estimation of poverty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monthly Per Capita Expenditure.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Monthly Per Capita Expenditure:-**

 
 
• 
 
It is used in economics and personal finance to describe the average monthly spending of each person in a defined population, such as a household, city, province, or country.

 
 
• 
 
This is calculated by taking the total monthly expenditure of the population and dividing it by the total number of people in that population.

 
 
• 
 
Formula:- **Monthly Per Capita Expenditure = Total monthly expenditure / Total population**.

 
 
• 
 
It can be referred to in the estimation of poverty.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marginal utility:-**

 
 
• It refers to the additional satisfaction or benefit (utility) that a consumer derives from consuming an additional unit of a good or service.
 
• The principle of diminishing marginal utility suggests that as a person consumes more and more of a good, the incremental benefit experienced from consuming another unit declines.
 
 
 
• **Minimum Support Price:-**
 
 
• It is generally used in the context of agricultural policies.
 
• MSP is a form of market intervention by the government to insure agricultural producers against any sharp fall in farm prices.
 
• The minimum support prices are announced by the government at the beginning of the sowing season for certain crops.

questions.question: Guru Shashadhar Acharya was awarded the Padma Shri in 2020 for his contribution to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhau dance.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chhau dance:-**

 
 
• **It is a form of tribal martial dance popular in the Indian states of Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal. **
 
• There are three subtypes of this dance, i.e., Seraikella Chhau, Mayurbhanj Chhau, and Purulia Chhau, named after the regions where they originated.
 
• This folk dance is unique and celebratory in spirit, often performed at festivals and religious events.
 
• It is famous for its masks, costumes, and high energy choreography, and it incorporates martial arts, acrobatics, and athletics.
 
 
 
• **Guru Shashadhar Acharya:-**
 
 
• He is a renowned Indian artist, primarily recognized for his contributions to Seraikella Chhau, a type of masked dance originating from the Seraikella region of Jharkhand.
 
• He has played a significant role in promoting and preserving the Seraikella Chhau tradition, teaching this art form to the next generations, ensuring its continuity and widespread recognition.
 
• **He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2020 for his contribution to Chhau dance.** 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Odissi Chaiti Ghoda dance:-**

 
 
• Chaiti Ghoda, or Chhau Ghoda, is a folk dance form from the eastern state of Odisha, India — specifically, the region of Kendrapara.
 
• It is a part of the traditional month-long worship of the goddess Durga during the month of Chaitra (March-April), which gives the dance its name.
 
 
 
• **Kathak:-**
 
 
• It is one of the eight forms of Indian classical dance, originating from northern India.
 
• Its name is derived from the Sanskrit word "katha" meaning story, and "katthaka" meaning the one who tells a story.
 
• Kathak focuses on rhythmic foot movements, adorned with small bells (Ghungroo), and the movement harmonizes with the music.
 
• This dance form includes pirouettes executed at lightning speed, complemented by subtle facial expressions.

questions.question: According to the Indian calendar, Vasanta Season falls in which months?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaitra-Vaisakha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian Calendar:-**

 
 
• It is also known as the "Saka calendar" or "Saka Samvat," which serves official and legislative purposes and is used alongside the Gregorian calendar.
 
• This calendar was introduced by the Calendar Committee in 1957, chaired by Meghnad Saha.
 
• The Saka calendar begins with the vernal (Spring) equinox of 78 Common Era (CE), designates its era as Saka Era, and counts years in that era.
 
• Chaitra is the first month of the year, and Phalguna is the last, aligning with the solar agricultural cycles.
 
• Vasanta Season falls in Chaitra-Vaisakha.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The months of the Indian National Calendar (Saka Samvat) are as follows:
 
 
• Chaitra (March 22 to April 21)
 
• Vaishakha (April 21 to May 22)
 
• Jyaistha (May 22 to June 22)
 
• Ashadha (June 22 to July 23)
 
• Shravana (July 23 to August 23)
 
• Bhadra (August 23 to September 23)
 
• Ashwin (September 23 to October 23)
 
• Kartika (October 23 to November 22)
 
• Agrahayana (November 22 to December 22)
 
• Pausha (December 22 to January 21)
 
• Magha (January 21 to February 20)
 
• Phalguna (February 20 to March 21)

questions.question: Which plant is considered a noxious weed that has a chemical defence mechanism to protect it from predators?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calotropis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Calotropis:-**

 
 
• **It is a genus of flowering plants in the family Apocynaceae.**
 
• It was first described as a genus in 1810.
 
• It is native to southern Asia and North Africa.
 
• They are commonly known as milkweeds because of the latex they produce.
 
• They are large shrubs growing to 4 m (13 ft) tall.
 
• **It is considered a noxious weed that has a chemical defence mechanism to protect it from predators**
 
 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17f4cb6618058e795dceecc3ca73e6bc53c96a6ca899666c7e8d766254e39f06.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chicory:-**

 
 
• It is scientifically known as Cichorium intybus.
 
• It is a somewhat woody, perennial herbaceous plant that usually has bright blue flowers.
 
• It originates from Europe and is now also found in North America and Australia.
 
• It's often seen growing along roadsides and in open fields.
 
• The plant is known for its long taproot, which is often ground into a powder and used as a coffee substitute or coffee additive.
 
 
 
• **Black henbane:-**
 
 
• It is scientifically known as Hyoscyamus niger, is a plant that originates from Eurasia.
 
• It's part of the nightshade family, which includes both poisonous and nonpoisonous plants such as tomatoes, potatoes, and belladonna.
 
• It's a biennial or short-lived perennial plant, with a strong, unpleasant odor.
 
 
 
• **Field bindweed:-**
 
 
• It is scientifically named Convolvulus arvensis, is a plant from the morning glory family.
 
• It is mostly perennial and native to Europe and Asia but has become widely distributed worldwide.
 
• It's known for being robust and difficult to control, characteristics that have made it quite problematic in agricultural settings where it is considered a significant weed.

questions.question: Who discovered that diborane reacts with aldehydes and ketones to produce dialkoxyboranes, Which are hydrolysed by water to produce alcohols?
questions.solution:

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** HC Brown:-**

 
 
• **Herbert C. Brown was a noted British-born American chemist.**
 
• He is best known for his work with organoboranes, a class of chemical compounds that contain a direct bond between carbon and boron. 
 
• Brown earned a B.S. degree in 1936 from Wright Junior College and then pursued his Ph.D. in Chemistry from the University of Chicago, which he received in 1938.
 
• **He discovered that diborane reacts with aldehydes and ketones to produce dialkoxyboranes.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Hugo Rudolph Kruyt :-**

 
 
• He was a Dutch chemist who significantly contributed to the field of colloid chemistry.
 
• Kruyt is known for his pioneering work in surface chemistry and is considered a founder of colloid science in the Netherlands.
 
 
 
• **Arthur Stoll:-**
 
 
• He was a Swiss scientist and chemist
 
• He is known for his significant contributions to the field of biochemistry, especially with regard to alkaloids.
 
 
 
• **Arne Tiselius:-**
 
 
• He was a notable Swedish biochemist who was awarded the Nobel Prize for Chemistry in 1948 for his groundbreaking research on electrophoresis and adsorption analysis.
 
• His pioneering techniques laid the foundation for later work on separation and purification methods for complex substances, especially proteins, in the biochemistry field.

questions.question: The origin of ‘Carnatic music’ is related to which of the following Dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijayanagar **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vijayanagar Dynasty:-**

 
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was a South Indian dynasty based in the Deccan Plateau region.
 
• **Established in 1336 by Harihara I and his brother Bukka Raya I of the Sangama Dynasty, the empire lasted until 1646, although its power declined after a major military defeat in 1565 by the Deccan sultanates.**
 
• The empire is named after its capital city of Vijayanagara, whose remains surround present-day Hampi, now a World Heritage Site in Karnataka, India.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was divided into various eras based on the ruling dynasty: Sangama Dynasty (1336–1485), Saluva Dynasty (1485–1505), Tuluva Dynasty (1505–1570), and the Aravidu Dynasty (1570–1646).
 
• **The origin of ‘Carnatic music’ is related to this Dynasty.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bahmani Sultanate:-**

 
 
• It is also called the Bahmanid Empire.
 
• It was a Muslim state in Deccan, India that lasted from 1347 to 1527.
 
• The Sultanate was founded by Alauddin Bahman Shah, a rebel officer who revolted against the Delhi Sultanate ruled by Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq.
 
• After gaining independence, Alauddin took the title of 'Bahman Shah', which led to the dynasty being named "Bahmani".
 
 
 
• **Chola Dynasty:-**
 
 
• 
 
It was a Tamil dynasty that ruled primarily in southern India until the 13th century.

 
 
• 
 
It was one of the longest-ruling dynasties in the world's history.

 
 
• 
 
The earliest datable references to the Chola are in inscriptions from the 3rd century BCE, left by Ashoka, of the Maurya Empire, and the dynasty continued to rule over varying territory until the 13th century CE.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Pandya Dynasty:-**

 
 
• 
 
It was also referred to as the Pandyas, an ancient Tamil dynasty that ruled extensive territories, at times including the large regions of South India, from their home base in Madurai.

 
 
• 
 
Historical records of the Pandyas trace back to the 3rd century BCE and they have been prominently referenced in the ancient Sangam Literature of the Tamil people.

questions.question: Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar and Mahadev Govind Ranade carried out their work of religious reforms in Maharashtra through which of the following organisations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Prarthana Samaj.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prarthana Samaj:**-

 
 
• The Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867 in Bombay by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang.
 
• It was an off-shoot of Brahmo Samaj.
 
• It was a reform movement within Hinduism and Justice M.G.
 
• **Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar joined it in 1870 and infused new strength to it.**
 
• **Mahadev Govind Ranade also ran the Deccan Education Society.**
 
• Several members of the Prarthana Samaj had earlier been active in the Paramhansa Mandali.
 
• This Samaj denounced idolatry, priestly domination, caste rigidities, and preferred monotheism.
 
• It also concentrated on social reforms like inter-dining, inter-marriage, widow remarriage, and the uplift of women and depressed classes.
 
• Apart from Hindu sects, it also drew upon Christianity and Buddhism.
 
• It sought truth in all religions.
 
• Drawing inspiration from the Maratha Bhakti saints of the medieval period, Ranade sought to establish the concept of one compassionate God.
 
• Veeresalingam Pantulu was the Telugu reformer who encouraged the Prarthana Samaj in South India.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atmiya Sabha:-**

 
 
• It tried to initiate social and religious reforms in society. 
 
• The association was a philosophical discussion circle in India.
 
• They used to conduct debate and discussion sessions on philosophical topics and also used to promote free and collective thinking and social reform.
 
• The foundation of Atmiya Sabha in 1815 is considered the beginning of the modern age in Kolkata.
 
 
 
• **Theosophical Society:-**
 
 
• It was founded by Madam HP Blavatsky and Col HS Olcott in New York in 1875.
 
• In 1882, its headquarters were shifted to Adyar (Tamil Nadu). 
 
• Theosophical Society of India was founded by Annie Beasant.
 
• The Theosophical Society sought inspiration from Indian thought and culture.
 
• It advocated the revival and strengthening of ancient religion of Hinduism, Zoroastrianism and Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Brahmo Samaj:-**
 
 
• It was formed in 1828
 
• It prohibited all forms of idolatry and sacrifice, believed in the Upanishads, and forbade its members from criticising other religious practices.
 
• It critically drew upon the ideals of religions – especially of Hinduism and Christianity – looking at their negative and positive dimensions.
 
• Brahmo ;Samaj discarded faith in divine Avatars.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of layers of Earth from the outside of the planet to the inside?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Crust (outermost) - mantle - core (innermost)__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **The Earth can be divided into several layers from the outermost to the innermost based on their compositional and physical properties. **
 
• The correct sequence is **Crust (outermost) - mantle - core (innermost)**.
 
 
• **Crust**:
 
 
• **This is the Earth's outermost layer, and it's where we live. **
 
• It's the thinnest layer, varying from about 5 kilometers in thickness in the oceanic crust to about 30-70 kilometers in the continental crust. The crust is largely composed of lighter rocks, such as granite and basalt.
 
 
 
• **Mantle**:
 
 
• **Beneath the crust, the mantle extends up to 2900 kilometers into Earth. **
 
• It is composed primarily of silicate rocks that are richer in iron and magnesium than the crust.
 
• The mantle can be divided further into the upper and lower mantle. The asthenosphere, a part of the upper mantle, behaves plastically due to the intense heat and pressure.
 
 
 
• **Outer Core: **
 
 
• **The outer core, lying beneath the mantle, is mostly composed of liquid iron and nickel. **
 
• This liquid layer is about 2200 kilometers thick and creates Earth's magnetic field due to its liquid state and its circulation movement.
 
 
 
• **Inner Core: **
 
 
• **The innermost layer, the inner core, is a solid ball consisting primarily of iron and nickel. **
 
• Despite the extremely high temperature, the enormous pressure at this depth keeps the material solid.
 
• The radius is around 1250 kilometers.
 
 
 
• Between each of these main layers, there are also transitional zones known as the lithosphere (between the crust and the mantle), the Gutenberg discontinuity (between the mantle and the outer core), and the Lehmann discontinuity (between the outer core and the inner core).

questions.question: Which of the following dances is NOT predominantly performed in the Indian state of Odisha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhavai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhavai**:-

 
 
• **Bhavai is a traditional, popular folk theatre form of the Indian state of Gujarat. **
 
• It is used as a medium to convey social messages and entertain audiences in villages and towns.
 
• Bhavai performances involve numerous acts, known as "veshas", depicting popular tales from Indian mythology, history, and contemporary social and political scenarios.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paika:- **

 
 
• The term "Paika" comes from the Odia word 'Paika', which means 'fighter' or 'warrior'.
 
• The Paikas were the traditional landed militia of Odisha, found in particular in the districts of Khurdha, Puri, and Cuttack.
 
• They served as warriors for the local kings or regional rulers, and in times of peace, they worked primarily as farmers.
 
 
 
• **Ghumra:-**
 
 
• **It **is a folk dance form native to the Indian state of Odisha, particularly prevalent in the Kalahandi district.
 
• Known for its rhythmic, energetic movements and beats, Ghumura dance draws its name from the Ghumura instrument, which is an earthen terracotta pot with both ends open, played by strapping it to the chest and beaten with two sticks.
 
 
 
• **Dhap:-**
 
 
• It is a folk dance form indigenous to the Mayurbhanj district of Odisha, India.
 
• This dance form was traditionally performed by the Kshatriya community (the warrior class in the traditional Indian caste structure), symbolizing the spirit of martial traditions and chivalry.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding removal of the President of India?

A. The impeachment process can be initiated in the either House of Parliament.

B. The impeachment charges must be signed by the one-third members of the House In which the process Is Initiated.

C. In the impeachment process, a 30 days’ notice should be given to the President.

D. The impeachment resolution is passed by a majority of two-thirds of the total membership of that House.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A and D only**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Impeachment of the President of India

 
 
• The President can be removed from office by a process of impeachment for violation of the Constitution.
 
• However, the Constitution does not define the meaning of the phrase violation of the Constitution.
 
• **The impeachment charges can be initiated by either House of Parliament. **
 
• **These charges should be signed by one-fourth of members of the House (that framed the charges), and a 14 days‘ notice should be given to the President.**
 
• The nominated members of either House of Parliament can participate in the impeachment of the President though they do not participate in his election. Hence, Statement 2 is not correct.
 
• The elected members of the legislative assemblies of states and the Union Territories of Delhi and Puducherry do not participate in the impeachment of the President though they participate in his election. 
 
• In the History of the Indian Republic, no Indian President has been so far "impeached" from his post.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to vote**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Right to vote:-**

 
 
• The right to vote in India is guaranteed by the Constitution and the Representation of the People Act, 1951, subject to certain limitations.
 
• Every citizen over the age of 18 has the right to vote under Article 326 of the Constitution.
 
• **The Right to vote in India is a Constitutional Right but not a fundamental right.**
 
• The 61st Amendment of the Constitution lowered the voting age of elections to the Lok Sabha and to the Legislative Assemblies from 21 to 18 years which was done by amending Article 326 of the Constitution.
 
• Article 326 of the Constitution guarantees universal adult suffrage but does not mention the right to vote.
 
• In India, voting is a legal right guaranteed by the Representation of People Act, 1950.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** The Right to Equality:-**

 
 
• It is one of the six fundamental rights of the Constitution. 
 
• It is contained in the Indian Constitution from Article 14 to 18. 
 
• Following are the provisions under the Right to Equality- 
 
 
• Article 14- ;equality before the law as well as equal protection of the law to all people.
 
• Article 15- prohibits discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth, and also gender or any of them. 
 
• Article 16- guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
 
• Article 17- Abolition of untouchability. 
 
• Article 18- Abolition of all titles except military and academic.
 
 
 
 
 
• Right to freedom of religion:-
 
 
• India is one of the most diverse nations in terms of religion.
 
• Freedom of religion in India is a fundamental right guaranteed by Article 25-28 of the Constitution of India.
 
• This right includes freedom to change his religion or belief and freedom, either alone or in community with others and in public or private, >to manifest his religion or belief, in worship, teaching practice and observance.

questions.question: When was the Smart Cities Mission launched in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2015.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Smart Cities Mission:-**

 
 
• The Smart Cities Mission is an urban renewal program launched by the Government of India with the mission to develop 100 cities across the country making them citizen friendly and sustainable.
 
• The Union Ministry of Urban Development is responsible for implementing the mission in collaboration with the state governments of respective cities.
 
• **The initiative was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 25 June 2015 with the government's intention to develop 'Smart Cities', a step towards improving the quality of life in urban cities and attracting people and investments to the cities.**
 
• The mission of the Smart Cities Mission is to drive economic growth and improve the quality of life of people in urban areas, by enabling local area development and harnessing technology, especially technology that leads to smart outcomes.
 
• Core infrastructure elements in a smart city would include:-
 
 
• **Adequate water supply,**
 
• **Assured electricity supply,**
 
• **Sanitation, including solid waste management,**
 
• **Efficient urban mobility and public transport,**
 
• **Affordable housing, especially for the poor,**
 
• **Robust IT connectivity and digitalization,**
 
• **Good governance, particularly e-Governance and citizen participation,**
 
• **Sustainable environment,**
 
• **Safety and security of citizens, particularly women, children and the elderly,**
 
• **Health and education.**

questions.question: The State of Kerala Vs Leesamma Joseph case deals with ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**persons with disabilities.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** State of Kerala Vs Leesamma Joseph:-**

 
 
• The Supreme Court of India in its judgment on 28 June 2021 in the case of "State of Kerala vs Leesamma Joseph" affirmed that persons with disabilities have a right to reservation in promotion under Article 16(4) of the Constitution of India, 1950.
 
• While examining the constitutionality of Section 33 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, the Court noted that 'equality of opportunity' in matters of public employment includes provision of certain reservations in favour of persons with disabilities.
 
• Furthermore, it held that Article 16(4) of the Constitution, empowering the State to make provisions for reservation in matters of promotion in favour of any backward class of citizens, also includes persons with disabilities within its scope, regardless of the nature of their establishments, whether they belong to the public sector or the private sector.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (RPDA):

 
 
• This is the principal legislation that protects the rights of individuals with disabilities in India.
 
• It replaces and strengthens the Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995.
 
• The RPDA complies with the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, to which India is a signatory.
 
• The Act expands the list of recognized disabilities from 7 to 21, and mandates the central and state governments to take measures to ensure that persons with disabilities fully enjoy all human rights and fundamental freedoms.
